title: Void Ending in an Opposition to Jupiter
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 4, Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The opposition is the hardest figure the Moon can close on: the text grades it as extreme enmity, because the signs it joins stand opposed across all four natural qualities. It shares with the square the warnings that guard every election, and a Moon waning in light and faced by Saturn is the source's own example of a serious misfortune.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with an opposition to Jupiter, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his temperate growth. Jupiter is the Great Fortune, hot and humid and temperate, the source of growing power: law, legality, jurisprudence, wisdom, the interpretation of dreams, and the ready winning of requests. His benevolence fits clergymen, kings, and lords; tin is his metal, the emerald and every shining white stone are his, and his animals are the beautiful and harmless ones once used for sacrifice. Set in the ascendant or at mid-heaven, the text says, he and Venus together rectify the Moon's misfortunes.
